title: time-decayed-touch-index-and-elastic-kv-lease-mutations
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: The current paged KV cache eviction and admission policies treat all touched entries with coarse recency counters, which leads to suboptimal reuse for interactive workloads with bursty prefixes. This causes either excessive evictions of hot prefixes or long-lived slots pinned by large cold contexts, increasing decode latency and tail variance.

Proposal: Implement a Time-Decayed Touch Index (TDTI) combined with Elastic KV Leases. TDTI stores a compact, exponentially decayed touch score per KV segment (quantized to 8 bits) that reflects both recency and frequency across minute-scale windows. Elastic Leases are temporary residency boosts (short leases) granted during prefill when a request pattern indicates strong near-term reuse. Leases mutate on observed reuse: successful reuses extend the lease; stalls or long-tailed misses shorten it. Together, TDTI+Leases enable: 1) admission decisions that favor segments with high short-horizon reuse probability; 2) graceful demotion of large cold segments; 3) low-cost background consolidation that coalesces adjacent hot microsegments.

Design details: - Touch indexing: use per-shard TDTI arrays with probabilistic updates on prefill and decode hits. Use a 1/1024 sampling for very-high-throughput shards to bound update cost. Decay factor alpha=0.85 per 15s epoch (configurable). Quantize to 8-bit and maintain a per-shard histogram for quick quantile queries. - Elastic Leases: leases are expressed as a small integer lease-token attached to a segment. Default lease length 30s (configurable). Grantation rules: prefill admission flow computes expected short-horizon reuse score from TDTI + request features (sequence length, model variant, kernel affinity). If score > Q75 then grant lease. Lease mutation occurs on decode: hit extends by +15s (capped); miss reduces remaining lease by 50% and penalizes admission score. - Background healing: low-priority consolidation process scans adjacency candidates using a lightweight bloom filter to avoid expensive scans. Merge threshold uses combined occupancy and TDTI slope metric. - Integration with kernel selection: when a lease is active, preference is given to kernel paths optimized for warm-KV fast-decode (reduced prefill latency); lease-aware kernel hints are surfaced in the routing metadata so runtime can co-place decode tasks with warm microblocks. - Safety: cap per-tenant total lease tokens to avoid eviction storms. Use admission backoff when memory pressure > 90% and fall back to deterministic LRU for a victim set.

Instrumentation and metrics: - TDTI distribution per shard (P10/P25/P50/P75/P90) - Lease grant rate, extend rate, and early-evict rate - Admission precision/recall over a 60s horizon (how many granted leases got reused) - Tail decode latency by lease-state (leased vs unleased) - Background consolidation CPU and memcpy usage

Acceptance criteria: - 10% reduction in 99th-percentile decode latency on interactive chat workload A (internal benchmark) at 70% memory occupancy - Lease grant precision >= 0.65 on production-sampled traffic after 2-week warmup - No user-facing errors or increased OOM incidents across canary fleet

Rollout plan: 1) Unit tests + simulation harness that replays production traces for TDTI and lease mutation logic. 2) Bench: microbench with synthetic workload to validate CPU overhead of updates (target < 2% extra CPU for prefill path). 3) Canary: enable in 5% of hosts in us-west-2 with telemetry gated to a new dashboard. 4) Gradual ramp to 50% then 100% with monitoring and automated rollback triggers (spike in OOM or >5% regression in tail latency).

Rollback steps: disable lease grants globally and revert admission flow to current LRU-prefill behavior; stop background consolidation; allow TDTI to decay naturally (no persistent state required).

Open questions: 1) Best decay epoch length for multimodal traffic (recommend experiments with 5s/15s/60s). 2) Quantization bias at 8 bits vs 12 bits and memory vs effectiveness tradeoff. 3) Interaction with dedicated/pinned capacity: should leases be sticky across restarts for Dedicated tenants?

Docs & artifacts: design doc (Confluence) https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/TDTI-design, PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821, benchmark dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/kv/tkti-canary-2025
comments: 2025-01-12 - Maya Chen: Initial spike: implemented TDTI prototype in simulation harness. Early results show better hot-segment recall on chat traces (precision ~0.6) but higher update CPU on small hosts. Added sampling knobs.
2025-01-20 - Luca Ortega: Reviewed prototype. Agreed to add per-shard sampling and histogram-based quantile query to keep hotpath cheap. Added background consolidation sketch using bloom filters.
2025-01-28 - SRE (Priya Nair): Canaries should include memory-pressure alarms and automated rollback on OOM. Added alerts and a canary checklist.
2025-01-31 - Performance (Jamal Rivera): Microbench results: TDTI updates add ~1.3% CPU at 50% sampling, 0.15% at 1/1024 sampling. Suggest default sampling 1/64 for medium tenants.
2025-02-02 - Luca Ortega: Merged simulation tests and opened runtime PR. Moving ticket to In Progress for canary deployment prep. Added TODO to evaluate decay epochs in AB tests.
